Five-minute quick start: tracks to scientific outputs

Source: vignettes/articles/quickstart-five-minutes.Rmd
quickstart-five-minutes.Rmd

Five-minute reproducible R analysis

Audience: first-time users familiar with basic R. Input: package-generated synthetic mathematical trajectories, not experimental fish videos. Output: plotted paths, one row per synthetic observation, a five-track summary, and CSV files. This exercise teaches the software contract; it does not validate real fish identification or tank measurements.

Step 1 — Install the published release

Use R 4.1 or later. Until the package is accepted on CRAN, install the official GitHub tag v0.1.1, not the unmerged 0.1.2 CRAN candidate.

install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("stefanosbalaskas/AquaTrajectories", ref = "v0.1.1")
library(aquaTrajectories)
packageVersion("aquaTrajectories")

Step 2 — Create and inspect five synthetic trajectories 

x <- aqt_simulate_tracks(n_fish = 5, n_frames = 120,
                         fps = 30, seed = 42)
stopifnot(inherits(x, "aqt_tracks"))
stopifnot(nrow(x) == 600L)
stopifnot(length(unique(x$track_id)) == 5L)
stopifnot(all(x$observed))
head(x[, c("session_id", "camera_id", "track_id",
           "time_s", "x", "y")])

Expected checks: 600 rows (5 × 120), five camera-scoped synthetic track labels, a time_s column, and a 2D tank-coordinate object. Values depend on the package’s deterministic mathematical random-walk generator, not a real dataset.

Step 3 — Plot and calculate motion 

aqt_plot_paths(x)
movement <- aqt_kinematics(x, max_gap_s = 0.05)
summary_by_track <- aqt_path_summary(x, max_gap_s = 0.05)
stopifnot(nrow(movement) == 600L)
stopifnot(nrow(summary_by_track) == 5L)
summary_by_track[, c("track_id", "valid_steps",
                     "path_length", "mean_speed")]

The step threshold of 0.05 seconds includes the 1/30-second synthetic cadence. Missing coordinates or longer gaps are not silently bridged. The simulated position unit is cm, but no biological swimming-speed calibration is implied.

Step 4 — Align a logged intervention 

events <- aqt_event_table(data.frame(
  session_id = "S01",
  event_id = "illustrative_feeding",
  start_s = 1,
  end_s = 2
))
aligned <- aqt_align_events(movement, events,
                            window_s = c(-1, 2))
head(aligned[, c("track_id", "event_id",
                 "relative_time_s", "phase")])

The event is an illustrative log entry. Alignment alone does not prove a feeding response or experimental treatment effect.

Step 5 — Export checkable outputs 

aqt_export_csv(x, "synthetic_tracks.csv")
utils::write.csv(summary_by_track,
                 "synthetic_path_summary.csv", row.names = FALSE)
utils::write.csv(as.data.frame(aligned),
                 "synthetic_event_alignment.csv", row.names = FALSE)

These files are written to the current R working directory. Verify their names and contents before sharing. To replace these synthetic paths with real observations, consult the starter CSV formats, video-to-results guide, and scientific capability matrix.

Common mistakes

Mistake Correction
Treating a tracker label as a permanent fish ID An ID is scoped by camera and session until externally verified
Calling an arbitrary z = 0 coordinate true 3D Image-only observations lack measured depth
Computing speed across unobserved frames Set a maximum admissible time gap and retain missingness
Treating every video frame as an independent replicate Experimental inference depends on actual randomized units (often tanks)
Calling the HMM state “stress” without ground truth Keep descriptive states separate from biological welfare inference

For full API help, use the reference index and scientific evidence dashboard.
